Mike: Quick sync 0m ago 16: run vs replay comparison turned up a p99 tail gap (~+120ms) only on replay traces. Synthetic loadbench looks fine. Anyone seen this pattern before?
Sara: Do we have exact batching and sequence distribution parity between the two runs? Small differences there change kernel picks.
Mike: I mirrored batch_size=8 and max_seq=1024. Synthetic sampling used UniDist, but replay is raw traces. Script used: `scripts/replay/compare_local.py` (I'll paste in a sec).
Deepak: Post the perf summary + kernel allocations. That'll quickly show whether a different kernel is used.
Mike: perf-dump snippet:
```
run: replay-2165439876 | model: gptx-16b | kernel: aten_cuda_fwd_v2 | p50: 24ms p95: 68ms p99: 142ms
run: synthetic-2165439876 | model: gptx-16b | kernel: cu_attn_opt | p50: 23ms p95: 60ms p99: 22ms
```
Mike: So replay frequently picks aten_cuda_fwd_v2; synthetic picks cu_attn_opt. That accounts for most of tail.
Jen: Selector heuristics use effective_seq and kv_occupancy to choose kernel. Long-tail contexts in replay could be pushing requests to aten kernel. Also, replay's request ordering creates KV warm states that don't appear in synthetic.
Kai: Also consider anonymization. If we replace PII with `<REDACTED>` we can shrink/grow token counts. What anon mode did you run?
Mike: I ran the anon pipeline in token-preserving mode this round. Haven't ruled out subtle tokenization differences though.
Deepak: Important: anonymization must be deterministic and token-length preserving for apples-to-apples. If you used proportional masks earlier, that could skew seq length distribution.
Mike: Noted. I'll re-run using strict token-preserve.
Sara: Separate axis: batching heuristics estimate occupancy using prior window token counts. Replay's burstiness and replays of long prefixes might produce higher kv_occupancy early in the request lifecycle and flip kernel choice.
Jen: We have selector debug flags. Run with `--kk-debug=reason,weights` to get per-request reason logs.
Mike: Ran it, sample logs:
```
[selector] req=abc reason=kv_occupancy>0.32
[selector] req=def reason=seq_len>512
[selector] kernel=aten_cuda_fwd_v2
```
Mike: Many requests show kv_occupancy in 0.3-0.45 during steps 1..8.
perf-bot: perf-diff: replay vs synthetic p99 delta +118ms (CI +/-4ms). kernel distro delta ~90% of difference.
Sara: Hypothesis: replay ordering + preserved prefixes -> early high kv occupancy -> selector chooses aten. Mitigations to try: (1) force cu_attn_opt for a controlled subset to measure perf and mem; (2) replay with randomized interleaving to mimic synthetic independence; (3) add KV-prefill mode to synthetic to emulate warm cache.
Deepak: Add deterministic seeds to anonymization and sampling (`--anon-seed`, `--sample-seed`). Otherwise non-determinism will change which kernel path is taken. Also record the RNG seed in metadata for reproducibility.
Mike: Pushed branch `replay/seeded-experiments` with flags and a small harness: `./run_compare.sh --seed 1337 --anon-mode=token-preserve` (link: github.com/redwood/replay/compare-seeds).
Jen: I did a quick A/B: forcing cu_attn_opt reduced p99 by ~110ms but raised p50 by ~2ms. No OOMs in 10k run; mem +3%.
Kai: Good but be cautious: cu_attn_opt may not be stable for very long seqs; check peak GPU memory and fragmentation. I'll run longer memory stress on Dedicated nodes.
Sara: For a strict apples-to-apples benchmark, we need these controls:
- tokenization/anon parity: use token-preserve mode and log anonymization transform hashes
- deterministic sampling: pin seeds for reservoir sampling and any stratification
- request order parity: either match synthetic ordering or explicitly document the replay ordering semantics
- KV state: define cold vs prefilled modes and expose `--kv-prefill=N` to populate per-trace KV before timing window
- capture kernel diagnostic logs: `--kk-debug=reason,kv_hist` and export `kernel_reason.csv`
- batch-window parity: ensure identical concurrency and inter-arrival times or replicate synthetic batching windows in replay harness
Deepak: Also instrument per-request checksums: compute `sha256(pre_anon_text)` and `sha256(post_serve_excerpt)` for a small sample to assert functional parity (no silent input changes) and help debug perf anomalies caused by content transforms.
Mike: I will run 3 experiments tomorrow:
A) replay-cold (baseline, no KV prefill, token-preserve, pinned seeds)
B) replay-prefill (KV prefill to emulate warm cache before measurement)
C) replay-prefill+order-randomized+pin-seeds (closest match to synthetic independence)
I'll attach perf dumps and `kernel_reason.csv` for each.
perf-bot: scheduled job 2165440000: compare-A-B-C-run; artifacts -> s3://redwood-replay/artifacts/2165440000/
Kai: For parity checks, include small golden set where we assert output tokens for first N steps to ensure selector changes don't alter numerical outputs (for model parity).
Jen: Also add reservoir sampling caps per-user to avoid heavy bias from a few monstrous traces. We saw earlier a single user with multiple 8k-token sessions skewing the kv occupancy histogram.
Mike: Filed bug ENG-RT-873: selector computing kv_occupancy using stale batch token counts; can cause misclassification for mid-range occupancy. Deepak, can you take it?
Deepak: I'll own ENG-RT-873. Plan: compute occupancy from live batch token counts and retest. If that reduces misroutes we'll fold into 0.27.1.
Sara: Great. Once runs complete, let's assemble a short methodology doc in `docs/replay/benching.md` describing canonical settings for apples-to-apples comparisons. Include the checklist above and example CLI calls.
Mike: Will do and will post results here. Thanks all.
Jen: Thanks 44d
Kai: Ping when artifacts land and I'll run Dedicated mem checks.
Mike: Will report back after runs complete.
